summary: Wall Street traders drove stocks higher and bond yields fell as more evidence of moderating inflation reinforced bets the Federal Reserve will refrain from raising interest rates next month.

title: Tapestry Beats Earnings but Faces Investor Disappointment Amid High Expectations
summary: Tapestry reported strong quarterly earnings driven primarily by its Coach brand, which accounted for $1.6 billion of the $1.9 billion in net sales and continues to deliver double-digit growth. Despite beating on many metrics and providing a revenue forecast in line with estimates for the new fiscal year, the stock fell sharply as investors were expecting more, especially after a 20% run-up prior to the report.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Container Shipping Companies Navigate Route Challenges
summary: Lee Klaskow, Senior Logistics Analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, discussed how container shipping companies are managing disruptions caused by route restrictions and geopolitical tensions. Despite only about a third of typical Suez Canal routes currently in use, companies remain confident that full utilization will resume over time, with alternative routes around Africa available if needed.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Goldman $2.25 Billion Neos Deal Raises Stakes in Active-ETF Race
summary: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s agreement to buy Neos Investments for as much as $2.25 billion marks a new front in Wall Street’s ETF battle: paying up for specialist firms that have found growth beyond the industry’s low-fee giants.

title: Why Private Funds Make Ann Berry Nervous
summary: Private-market investing is becoming more accessible, but Ann Berry,  Threadneedle Ventures Founder, is warning investors not to confuse accessibility with transparency. She joined Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why valuing private companies requires specialized expertise, why ordinary investors may struggle to assess the underlying businesses, and why these new publicly traded funds require extraordinary trust in their managers. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AMD to Raise as Much as $5 Billion From Debt Offering
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. is planning to raise as much $5 billion in what would be the chipmaker’s biggest-ever US dollar investment-grade bond sale, adding to a wave of debt tied to the artificial intelligence boom.

title: India Urea Offers Decline 12% as War Supply Squeeze Eases
summary: India, one of the world’s biggest urea importers, received offers for the soil nutrient that were 12% below the June purchase price, signaling that the war-driven tightness in the global fertilizer market is easing.

title: Why Romantasy May Soon Be a Billion-Dollar Business
summary: Romantasy has grown from a BookTok-driven obsession to a nearly billion-dollar business, powered by a largely female fandom scooping up special editions, merchandise, event tickets, audiobooks and more. The genre's rise is reshaping publishing and drawing retailers, creators and now Hollywood into one of the book industry’s most powerful new markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Entry-Level, White-Collar Jobs to See 'Massive' AI Impact, Says Virginie Maisonneuve
summary:
The number of employers who expect entry-level workers to be AI-competent has nearly tripled since last fall, according to the National Association of Colleges and Employers. 
Workers’ anxiety about AI has surged, along with demand for quick training programs.
Virginie Maisonneuve, Founder at Maisonneuve Global Advisors, discusses inflation, rates, and the dual impact of AI on prices and the labor market. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Birkenstock Rallies on Forecast; StubHub Falls on Earnings | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- StubHub (STUB) shares are dropping after the company reported earnings per share for the second quarter that missed the average analyst estimate. 
- Birkenstock (BIRK) is rallying after the footwear maker boosted its adjusted Ebitda forecast for the full year. The German company also reported better-than-expected sales for the second quarter. 
- Cerebras (CBRS) is lower after the company projected slower growth than some investors anticipated, causing its shares to fall in premarket trading. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Traders Pare Bets on Fed Rate Hike This Year as Oil Prices Fall
summary: Bond traders stopped fully pricing in a Federal Reserve interest-rate increase this year amid a retreat in oil prices that reinforced positive sentiment on the inflation outlook.

title: La Caisse Posts 5% First-Half Return as Stocks Rally, Private Equity Slumps
summary: Caisse de Depot et Placement du Quebec, Canada’s second-largest pension manager, fell short of its benchmark in the first half of the year as losses on private equity holdings pulled down the overall return.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 13
summary: Oil snapped its run of recent gains, as limited progress over a deal to end the Iran war left traders parsing how much oil is crossing the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Airlines Reflect Our Economic Future
summary: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Allison Schrager explains why increasingly stratified airline fares offer a glimpse into the future of the US economy, where technology could mean more personalized prices and an even wider range of goods and services. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Old Mutual Shares Trade Again in Zimbabwe After Six-Year Halt
summary: Shares in Old Mutual Ltd. began trading on Zimbabwe’s dollar-denominated stock exchange, six years after they were suspended on the country’s main bourse to curb a currency rout.

title: Odd Lots: Trucking Is Booming and Drivers Aren’t Happy About It
summary:
In the last year, freight companies have seen a significant upturn in business. But in addition to growing demand, the industry has also experienced new constraints on the supply side, with the US administration cracking down on who is even allowed on the road.

Reed Loustalot, chief marketing officer at the Truck Parking Club, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss the booming trucking business and the crackdown on the supply side of the market. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Foreign Investors Flee Brazil Stocks at Fastest Pace Since 2021
summary: Foreign investors pulled money out of Brazilian equities on Tuesday at the fastest pace in over five years as concerns over the presidential election make them increasingly wary of the outlook for the fiscal deficit and the economy.
